§13.1 Chemical Molecules

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

other-chemical-molecules · other rule images diagrams math

✅ Normative

Linear formulae, ions and reactions MUST be written with \ce{...}, and drawn structures, rings and branches with \chemfig{...}. Standalone chemical markup MUST be placed in a fenced latex block. Legible structure MUST be preserved; an unreadable portion MUST be described rather than guessed.

Structural formulae and reaction equations printed as figures.

A structural formula printed as a figure — exactly the case a prose description cannot reconstruct.

Which markup

The markup follows what is printed:

Printed Markup Examples
A formula, ion or reaction written on a line mhchem — \ce{...} \ce{SO4^2-}, \ce{2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O}
A 2D molecular structure: rings, branches, drawn bonds chemfig — \chemfig{...} a ring with its substituents

Why a code representation rather than a description

A structural formula is exactly reconstructable — unlike a photograph, it has a canonical textual encoding that a chemist or a downstream tool can render back to the same picture. A prose description ("a benzene ring with a hydroxyl group") is lossy and unverifiable, and it silently discards stereochemistry, charges and substituent positions. A legible structure therefore MUST NOT be rendered as prose.

The same reasoning governs Electrical Schematics§12.2.3 and Blueprints§12.2.1: a domain-specific code block is preferred wherever a faithful one exists.

Placement and unreadable structures

  • A formula standing on its own — a displayed structure or reaction — MUST be in a fenced latex block.
  • Every legible atom, bond, charge and substituent MUST be kept (never drop).
  • Where part of a structure cannot be read, that part MUST be described in words, and the output MUST NOT fill it in with a plausible guess (never invent).
